html:
The Revolt of the Comuneros was a long rising of Spanish settlers in Paraguay against royal governors and the Jesuits, from 1721 to 1735.

The settlers of Asunción resented the Jesuit missions, which kept the Guarani labour they wanted and sold yerba mate in competition with them. They backed a governor, José de Antequera, against the viceroy in Lima. He was arrested and executed in 1731, but the revolt went on, with the settlers claiming the right of the commune to choose its own rulers.

Troops from Buenos Aires crushed it in 1735. It was among the first challenges to Spanish rule in South America, and later Paraguayans saw it as an early step towards independence. It also helped turn opinion in Spain against the Jesuits, who were expelled from Spanish America in 1767.
sum: The Revolt of the Comuneros was a long rising of Spanish settlers in Paraguay against royal governors and the Jesuits, from 1721 to 1735.
